# 05 Close the board: the example, the glossary, the numbers

## Outcome

An author can see all fourteen shapes without reading a test, and the records say what changed —
including the one documented token that quietly stopped reaching most nodes.

## Why this ticket exists

Thirteen shapes landed. The example that shows them is how anyone finds out, and two durable
records are now wrong or incomplete.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] An example draws **every** shape, rendering with **zero diagnostics** — not merely zero
      errors. Decide whether it extends an existing example or is a new file, and say why; the
      repo's own precedent is that `complex-showcase.srn` and `flowchart-styling.srn` each keep
      one story, and board 4's `flowchart-syntax.srn` was a new file for that reason.
- [x] The `examples/` enumeration test covers it automatically. Confirm rather than assume.
- [x] **Assert the example against its own text as well as its picture.** Board 4's ticket 07
      found its example test passed even when the example was rewritten longhand — a picture
      assertion alone would not stop this file losing the shapes it exists to demonstrate.
- [x] A demo page shows them. Check whether an existing flowchart demo should gain it rather than
      adding a page nobody links to; board 4's closing ticket noted `flowchart-syntax.srn` never
      got one, so decide that too and say which.
- [x] `CONTEXT.md`'s **Node** entry stops saying a node has exactly one shape, and names the
      fourteen. Mind the `_Avoid_` lines.
- [x] **`CONTEXT.md` records that `--siren-node-border-radius` no longer reaches most shapes —
      and note after ticket 03 that this has TWO halves, for two different reasons.** It stops
      reaching a `<path>` frame because `rx` means nothing on a path (board decision 4). It also
      stops reaching a round node and a stadium, which ARE rects, because ticket 03 gave them an
      inline radius of their own so no token could flatten a stadium's semicircular ends. The
      first is a consequence; the second is a decision. Both belong in one paragraph, and a
      consumer needs to be told which shapes the token still reaches: the rectangle and the
      subroutine, and after ticket 04 possibly nothing else.
      The theme sets `rx` on `.siren-node-frame`, which does nothing on a `<path>` or `<ellipse>`.
      That is correct — a diamond has no rounded corners — but it is a documented token silently
      narrowing its reach, which a consumer needs told.
- [x] `.dev/mermaid-diagram-roadmap.md` marks this board done and names what is next, with the
      contract-change classification the previous roadmap entry established.
- [x] `.dev/mermaid-compatibility-gaps.md` updated to the board's final numbers.
- [x] **State the board's starting and final corpus counts**, and confirm no `fc-shape-*` row is
      still `rejected`. The three `silently-wrong` rows must be exactly the three this board
      inherited — if one moved, that is a finding, not a rounding.

## On the ratchet numbers in this ticket

They are an **expectation, not a quota.** Ticket 01 found a real compatibility gap and declined to
fix it because adding a corpus row would have pushed `REJECTED` one above the number its ticket
named. That was an honest reading of a badly written instruction: the ratchet exists to stop
regressions, not to stop progress.

So: if you discover a gap, **add the row and say so**. `rejected` rising because a new gap was
measured is the same legitimate case as `silently-wrong` rising in board 4 — a measurement was
corrected, not code made worse. State which in your report, and move the literal to whatever the
suite actually produces.

- [x] **Found by ticket 04.** `contracts.ts`'s `NodeShape` doc says "a spelling whose ticket has
      not landed is still refused by the parser". Every spelling has landed, so the sentence is now
      vacuous. One line; that file was outside ticket 04's scope.
- [x] **Found by ticket 04, worth a roadmap line.** `fc-text-markdown` is the only thing keeping
      `UNIMPLEMENTED_LABEL_FORMS`, `unimplementedFormIn`, `BRACKET_FORM_RE` and
      `refuseUnimplementedForm` alive. When it lands they all go together, and the table's doc
      already says so — record it where the next planner reads it.
- [x] **Found by ticket 04.** `A(())` and `A[()]` parse here as an empty circle and an empty
      cylinder; mermaid 11.17.2 rejects both, probed. Siren accepting more than Mermaid is safe
      (the condition runs one way), and `A()` has always behaved this way — but nobody has measured
      it. Decide whether it earns a corpus row or a roadmap line.

Corpus re-measured at both endpoints: **32/33/3 at board open → 46/22/3 now**, no `fc-shape-*`

Caught two planner errors: the packet's opening counts were transposed (it measured `f0b2296`
